Taipei 101. The 101-story supertall skyscraper completed in 2004 in Taipei, Taiwan, rising 1,667 feet and holding the world's tallest-building record for six years. Its segmented pagoda-inspired design incorporates traditional Chinese architectural language with cutting-edge wind-resistance engineering. Designed by Taiwanese architect C.Y. Lee, the tower's form divides into eight segments representing the number eight, which is auspicious in Chinese culture and reinforces the connection between tradition and modernity. At 508 meters tall, it surpassed the Petronas Twin Towers and held the record until the Burj Khalifa opened in 2010. The tower features a massive tuned mass damper of 660 tons that moves in response to wind and earthquakes, making it one of the world's most seismically engineered buildings. The facade uses a golden-green tinted glass that references Taiwan's landscape and reduces heat absorption in the subtropical climate. It houses office space, luxury residences, and a shopping mall, with the observation deck on the eighty-ninth floor serving as a major tourist attraction. Completed at the peak of Taiwan's economic expansion, it serves as a symbol of the island's technological prowess and cultural confidence.
